newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard was last night forced to admit Australia's high unemployment rate was unlikely to fall until at least next year, following the release of figures showing a rise in the unemployment rate from 8.7 per cent to 8.8 per cent, and a drop in employment of 40,300 in May, the highest drop since October 1995. The poor figures have prompted further calls for another cut in interest rates. Page 1.

Under deals worth US$3 billion, Rupert Murdoch's News Corp now has a stake in the North American satellite TV industry and has taken control of the International Family Entertainment cable network. News Corp will join with Time Warner, Comcast Corp and Tele-Communications Inc in US satellite TV provider PrimeStar. Page 31.

Brokers JB Were, SBC Warburg, First Pacific and County NatWest were amongst those who have benefited from strong share trading, through large deals such as the Foster's Brewing deal, the listing of Colonial Mutual and National Mutual, and the final sale of shares in the Commonwealth Bank. However, for many other major and second-rate brokers, earnings for the year to June will be solid but unspectacular. Page 32.

In a move that takes place as it prepares for its demutualisation, the Australian Stock Exchange will review its policy of charging royalties on Internet live share prices, following pressure from stockbrokers and information providers who say the existing royalties impede online share trading. Page 32.

Dairy and fruit juice business National Food Ltd managing director Max Ould said yesterday the company will relocate its head office and its milk and international divisions to Melbourne under further overhauls of its business. Ould said the move will no generate savings, but will allow a greater management focus on its two core businesses. Page 33.

Papua New Guinean mining company Highlands Pacific Ltd yesterday listed on the Australian Stock Exchange, with investors enjoying a modest 2 per cent gain. At the close of trade yesterday, 2.6 million shares were traded and the share price gained two cens to A$1.02. Page 33.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite a rise in shares of around 7 per cent in The News Corp, ratings agency Standard & Poors flagged a credit downgrade for the company following its US$3 billion expansion into the United States pay TV market. S&P argued the United States acqusitions would require heavy cash funding for the next few years. Page 23.

Following the releases of figures showing the largest drop in employment in one month for four years, along with other poor economic figures, financial markets were yesterday buzzing with speculation of further interest rate cuts. Page 23.

Shares in the ANZ Bank rose as high as 8 per cent yesterday on the back of speculation it is being targeted by a foreign predator. The sharp increase prompted the Australian Stock Exchange to question the Bank, which said it knew of no reason for the shae gains. Page 23.

Camelot Resources announced yesterday it has successfully raised A$57.5 million thanks to the underwriting of a A$25 million convertible note issue by a Swiss institution and Teck Corp of Canada TEK.TO. The move allows Camelot to take its 50 per cent share of Mt Edon Gold Mines. Page 24.

The West Australian Government has come under fire from United States-owned gas pipeline group PGT Australia, which says the Government had effectively blocked its plans to spend A$1 billion building a pipeline in Australia. New South Wales-based energy group AGL also criticised the Government for the awarding of the only MidWest Iron and Steel project contract to Epic Energy. Page 25.

In a move that is likely to push the price of copper above yesterday's 12 month high, Ok Tedi Mining, which is 53 per cent owned by BHP, warned it may need to shut down its copper and gold milling operation in Papua New Guinea because of a prolonged dry spell. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian dollar slumped to just US75.21 cents following the release of figures showing a drop in employment in May, which indicate the Australian economy is still in a rut. The figures have prompted some economists to predict the Reserve Bank may anounced another official cut in interest rates as early as today. Page 25.

Cable & Wireless deputy chief executive Rod Olsen is one contender possibly in line for the position of chief executive of Optus Communications, which is expected to be vacated by Ziggy Switkowski today. While speculation over the resignation of Switkowsi has been rife for over a month, Optus Communications has still refused to comment on the issue. Page 25.

In a move indicating a play for control of troubled food ingredients group Burns, Philp & Co, A$130 million was spent by an overseas buyer on more than 10 per cent of the company. A price of A$2.50 a share was paid for the purchase, which is 47 cents mor than Burns Philp's market price. Page 25.

Communications Minister Richard Alston admitted to a Senate estimates committee yesterday Telstra and Optus Communications may have to stop building mobile phone towers and deploying their pay TV in three weeks if the State Governments do not establish alernative planning processes by July 1. Page 27.

Reserve Bank deputy governor Graeme Thompson warned yesterday bank lending standards had slipped significantly over the past couple of years, and this may lead to future credit quality problems. However, Thompson said a repeat of the 1980s and early 1990s when loose lending by the banks led to writing of A$25 million in loan losses, would not occur. Page 27.

Aristocrat founder Len Ainsworth is suing Blackbird Gaming, a private family trust company run by his son Kjerulf, for allegedly breaching a shareholder agreement made with the trust companies of Mr Ainsworth's seven sons. The agreement allowed for 80 pe cent of the proceeds from the selling of any shares by any family member to go to Mr Ainsworth. Page 27.
THE AGE

Shares in the ANZ Bank were at one stage over A$10 on the back of speculation it may be the subject of a foreign bid. While the ANZ denied any knowledge of a takeover, speculation centred on a European bank lodging a takeover application with the Foreign Investment Board to buy ANZ with ABN Amro, ING Barings, National Westminster Bank and Lloyds TSB the most likely contenders. Page B1.

Sources close to Optus Communications said yesterday the company will today announce the departure of chief executive Ziggy Switkowski, who has been with Optus for only one year. It is believed Switkowski would be replaced by current chief operating officer Phil Jacobs until a permanent replacement is found. Page B1.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corp yesterday announced it would pay United States evangelist Pat Robertson US$1.9 billion in cash for International Family, which owns cable-TV service, The Family Channel. The move will see News Corp with a service in all ive major cable formats: movies, news, entertainment, sports and children. Page B1.

National Australia Bank failed in a bid to claim a $42 million tax deduction when the Federal Court dismissed the bank's appeal against a ruling by the taxation commissioner assessing the amount as a capital payment. NAB paid the money to the Federal Govrnment in 1991 for exclusive rights to make subsidised home loans to Defence Force personnel. Page B3.

Burns Philp & Co moved closer towards a takeover bid after an individual raider spent $130 million for a 10 per cent stake. Paying $2.50 a share, 43 cents above its closing price, this latest development comes after Burns' decision to sell its herbs and pices assets in North America and Europe, further fuelling market speculation of a takeover. Page B3.

A legal dispute between Country Road retail group and Mr Solomon Lew, who holds 9.2 per cent of Country Road, was held over until June 19 by a Supreme Court judge. Mr. Lew is claiming that the retail group is in breach of a 20-year lease on a property tht runs to 2006. Page B3.
